corrected_verdict: CITATION_FOUND (prefer Parkinson-Ongie-Willett SIMODS 2025 over the unpublished Ongie-Willett 2022 arXiv; Srebro 2004 Lemma 1 is the load-bearing citation)
issues: All three checker citations exist, have correct bib fields and say what is claimed. Srebro-Rennie-Jaakkola NIPS 17 (2004): Lemma 1 is the trace norm = min over X=UV' of 1/2(||U||_F^2+||V||_F^2). Ongie-Willett arXiv 2202.00856: Lemma 3.2, q=2/(L-1), and L=3 gives the nuclear norm. It is arXiv-only (v1, no journal-ref), so the checker's 'venue unconfirmed' is right. Gunasekar 2017 is correct but tangential (implicit gradient-descent bias, not an explicit price). MISSED: the peer-reviewed successor, Parkinson, Ongie, Willett, SIAM J. Math. Data Sci. 7(3):1021-1052 (2025), DOI 10.1137/24M1672158, arXiv 2305.15598. Its Lemma 2.1 is the same result and it cites Srebro 2004 for the two-factor case, so cite it instead of or next to the 2022 preprint. Recht-Fazel-Parrilo SIAM Rev. 2010, Lemma 5.1 / problem (5.1), is an optional canonical alternative to Srebro. SCOPE: the Ongie/Parkinson formulas are for 1-homogeneous ReLU units, so their a-vs-W rebalancing does not transfer to degree-nu product neurons. Only the linear-algebra fact (shared layer times neuron weights under Frobenius cost gives a nuclear norm, Srebro Lemma 1) transfers, so Srebro is load-bearing. GLOSS: no source says the nuclear norm 'rewards carrying many frequencies in one neuron'. The nuclear norm is invariant under left-orthogonal mixing, so it is indifferent to how frequencies are spread over neurons, and 'rewards' overstates it. Consider 'does not penalize'. TOOLING (workflow slowness): the session WebSearch budget is exhausted (200/200), so every remaining verifier runs without search. dblp times out at 60 s, Semantic Scholar returns 429, WebFetch cannot parse PDFs, and all verifiers share one scratchpad with colliding file names.

extra_citations.why: Peer-reviewed successor of Ongie-Willett 2022 (arXiv 2305.15598). Lemma 2.1: weight decay on L-1 linear layers in front of ReLU units equals a Schatten-q price, q=2/(L-1), on the virtual inner weight matrix, so one linear layer gives the nuclear norm. The intro states the nuclear-norm equivalence explicitly.
Optional canonical alternative to Srebro 2004: problem (5.1), min 1/2(||L||_F^2+||R||_F^2) s.t. A(LR')=b, is equivalent to nuclear-norm minimization (Lemma 5.1).
